measured: 2026-10-13, production build (next build, next start on localhost:3300), headless Chrome 154 over the DevTools protocol. LAB DATA ONLY: one machine, synthetic loads and inputs. No field data, no real device, no Safari, not Lighthouse.

method.lcp: PerformanceObserver largest-contentful-paint, median of 3 fresh loads in a new tab, cache disabled
method.layoutShift: sum of layout-shift entries without recent input, at load and after a scroll to the foot of the page and back
method.throttling: slow 4G: 150 ms latency, 1.6 Mbit/s down, 750 kbit/s up; CPU slowdown as named in each profile
method.clip: media events (playing, waiting, ended) timed from navigation start. One 'waiting' at about 0.06 s is the clip starting, also seen with no throttling; more than one is a visible stall
method.geometry: getBoundingClientRect with prefers-reduced-motion set, so the showcase shows its poster
method.interaction: real key presses, touch taps and clicks dispatched through the DevTools protocol

caveats: With no throttling at 1440px Chrome reports the clip's first frame as the LCP element, as in the earlier rounds; the poster is already painted by then.
prefers-reduced-data could not be emulated in this Chrome (the media query did not match); the Save-Data and 2G paths were tested through navigator.connection.
The drawn page's clip loops, so it has no 'ended' time.
Stock media: three assets from three unrelated places. The numbers say how photographs and film of this weight behave in this layout, not how VNest's own will look.

illustratedPageUnchanged.note: Today's drawn page against the 12/10 captures in ../refine-01, pixel by pixel. Every differing pixel is either on an edge inside the showcase picture (the 12/10 captures show the clip's first frame over the poster; today's show the poster alone) or in the section frame below the fold (its arrival animation is skipped under reduced motion). Layout, type, frames and the booking action are identical.
